source: NASA Space Apps challenge text: 'Places on Earth that have analogous characteristics to the Moon or Mars - the Atacama Desert, Haughton Crater, Death Valley'

results.note: Very dry desert terrain, used for testing rovers and methods for dry Martian surfaces.
results.summary: Predicted good analog (67 percent probability of a good analog). Pushes toward good: above-average avg solar index and above-average max slope. Pushes toward poor: above-average avg slope angle.

results.note: Cold polar desert inside an impact crater, used for field tests of exploration equipment and operations.
results.summary: Predicted good analog (66 percent probability of a good analog). Pushes toward good: above-average max temperature swing. Pushes toward poor: below-average avg solar index and above-average avg slope angle.

results.terrain: hot arid basin, salt flats, alluvial fans
results.note: Hot, arid basin with large daily temperature swings and varied rocky terrain.
results.summary: Predicted good analog (90 percent probability of a good analog). Pushes toward good: above-average max slope and above-average avg solar index. Pushes toward poor: above-average avg slope angle.
